method: Data: the gnn_opt harness CV on night_train, with identical rows and folds for every predictor: 3,370 eval==1 rows, 135 positives, 64 configs, 128 runs, 18 folds from gnn_opt/folds.json (2x5 grouped ID folds + 8 LODO folds). Scores: repeat-averaged ID out-of-fold predictions (harness.id_oof, as in evaluate.py --pairs). Zero-shot LLM scores are the same in every fold. Inference unit: config. Paired nonparametric cluster bootstrap over the 64 configs, B = 10,000 resamples (numpy default_rng seed 20261108). All predictors and statistics use the same config draws, so every difference is paired. The bootstrap is computed exactly from config multiplicities k as AUROC(k) = k'Mk/((k'n1)(k'n0)), where M[c,c'] counts positive-in-c > negative-in-c' pairs (ties 0.5). This was validated against sklearn and the harness time_matched_auroc on the full sample and on concatenated resamples (max |diff| 1.1e-16). With evaluate.py's own draws (seed 0, n = 1000), it reproduces the --pairs quantiles bit for bit. Statistics: (a) the harness time-matched AUROC (AUROC within round bins 1-5, 6-10, ..., 26-30, weighted by #positives; bins 1-10 hold no positives) and (b) pooled ID AUROC. Estimate = full-sample difference A-B. 95% CI = 2.5/97.5 percentiles of the bootstrap differences. Two-sided p = 2*min(P*(d<=0), P*(d>=0)), floored at 1/B = 1e-4. Multiplicity: Holm over the 11 pre-registered primary comparisons: 5 communication monitors vs clock on tAUROC, plus gnn_final, gnn_hybrid and zs:pairwise vs bag+graph, zs:pairwise vs gnn_final and gnn_hybrid, and zs:global_full vs bag+graph on AUROC. For each comparison the report also gives the number of the 8 LODO folds with the same sign (computed from fold-specific LODO predictions) and an exact two-sided binomial sign test. The sign test is descriptive only, because the LODO folds overlap. Sensitivities, each with its own Holm: the plan's rounds-to-cut time bins (pairs-weighted) for (a); the per-repeat-mean AUROC (harness ID_AUROC definition) for (b); and a seed-aware SE that adds the single-model GNN seed variance (normal approximation). Row-level DeLong (Sun & Xu) is reported only as a contrast. Secondary analyses use no multiplicity correction (plan §9) and the same bootstrap. They compare GNN controls and ablations (id0, seed 0) with the matched reference m_noer id0 (same config {epochs 30, edge_readout off}, seed 0). The seed-noise floor comes from s_base/s_base_r1/s_base_r2 (seeds 0/100/200) and from m_noer_swa and m_tmemgru, seed 0 vs seed 100 ('seed 2'). A difference counts as exceeding seed noise if its seed-aware 95% CI (Δ ± 1.96·sqrt(SE_boot² + 2σ²_seed)) excludes 0. The report also shows whether it exceeds the largest observed seed |Δ| and the t-band.

results.conclusion: Single-model seed noise on id0 is as large as most architecture differences. Of the 22 screen variants only s_gtemp_none (no temporal block, -0.086 [-0.148, -0.024], seed-aware CI [-0.167, -0.006]) clears it. None of the 18-fold m_* differences does (e.g. m_tmemgru - m_noer -0.020 [-0.048, +0.003]).

caveats: night_train only: 64 configs, 3,370 rows, 135 positive rows from 45 tipped runs in 26 configs (at most 6 positives per config). A percentile bootstrap with 64 clusters can under-cover a little, so p-values near 0.05 are approximate. The p floor is 1e-4 and the Holm floor 0.0011.

This is not the plan's full decision rule. ANALYSIS_PLAN §4 also needs sign agreement in at least 3 of 4 held-out splits (protocol b) and protocol (a) over all night configs. Here only the harness CV on night_train was evaluated. LODO sign counts are a within-CV proxy, and the overlapping LODO folds make the sign test descriptive. Test splits were not touched.

Zero-shot LLM monitors read raw message text, including task words and the shortcut lexicon. Those are ablation-only inputs for the headline GNN and bag+graph, so part of the LLM advantage may be lexical access.

zs:global_full sees the whole transcript from round 1, which acts as an implicit clock (Spearman rho with t = 0.83, the highest of all predictors). Time-matched AUROC controls for it only coarsely (5-round bins).

The monitor model (Claude Haiku 5.5) is also one of the two jury judges (DeepSeek V4 Flash + Claude Haiku 5.5) whose ratings form the GNN and bag+graph features. The monitor families are not independent views.

The zero-shot monitors are untrained. Their LODO numbers are subset AUROCs, not transfer tests, so their selection score means something different. Prompt development used 8 night_train dev runs (frozen at r0, no revisions), and those runs are part of the evaluated rows.

The repeat-averaged OOF gives trained models a 2-model mini-ensemble; the zero-shot scores do not get one. The per-repeat sensitivity changes no Holm verdict and slightly favours the zero-shot monitors.

The config-bootstrap CIs exclude training-seed and LLM-sampling noise. The seed-aware sensitivity changes no verdict. LLM sampling noise was measurable only for global_full (single sample vs k = 3: -0.005 AUROC [-0.013, +0.003]), not for pairwise (k = 1).
The clock is a weak bar time-matched: hgb_clock tAUROC is 0.401 with round bins and 0.635 with rounds-to-cut bins. All monitors also beat 0.5.
Secondary analyses use id0 only (5 folds, one seed), and seed noise is estimated from few seed pairs (4 df on id0, 2 df on 18 folds). No multiplicity correction (plan §9).

gnn_final = final.csv (verified: probability mean of m_noer_swa and m_tmemgru with 2 seeds each). RESULTS.md mentions a better node-GRU GNN that is not the shipped model and is not tested here. The plan's 'gnn_final = ____' field is still empty.
Deviations from the plan: B = 10,000 instead of 1,000. Harness round-bin tAUROC is primary and the plan's rounds-to-cut bins are the sensitivity; the verdicts are identical under both.
The task described zs_tip as 0-100, but in the data it is already divided by 100 (0-1). AUROC is unaffected. Brier is not meaningful for the uncalibrated zero-shot scores.
